notes: 5–6 focused hours on regular and review days. C/P priority. Full lengths and final taper have separate workloads.

phases.name: Rebuild fundamentals
phases.details: Focused untimed UWorld sets. C/P every study day. Learn the concept, apply it, then explain the error without notes.

phases.name: Build mixed practice
phases.details: Move from topic sets to mixed section sets. Begin timed practice without sacrificing review. Continue daily C/P repair.

phases.name: AAMC practice and timing
phases.details: Prioritize available AAMC Section Bank, Question Packs and unused exams. Use UWorld for targeted gaps. Timed science blocks build to 59 questions in 95 minutes.

phases.name: Consolidate weaknesses
phases.details: Finish final exam review, revisit recurring mistakes and strengthen recall. No new resource or large new Anki deck.

phases.name: Taper and rest
phases.details: Reduce workload, protect sleep and prepare test-day logistics.

study_rules: Times are focused study time; take 5–10 minute breaks between blocks and a meal break. A 330-minute study day takes longer than 5.5 hours on the clock.
Question counts are targets, not quotas. If review takes longer, reduce new questions and use that time for review. Do not skip explanations to finish a count.
For each missed or guessed answer: identify the tested concept, locate passage evidence, explain why your choice fails, and write one prevention rule. Make only 1–2 short cards for reusable gaps.
C/P: write the governing relationship and units before calculating. Practice rearranging equations and estimating without a calculator.
Early practice: untimed and untutored, reviewing after each small set. Use tutored mode when learning a new topic. Later timed blocks: no notes, hints or answer checking.
Anki: prioritize due cards and missed-question concepts. Cap work at the scheduled time; reduce new cards if reviews become unmanageable.

Each Sunday checkpoint: compare similar unused sets, identify the three most repeated errors and replace next week’s repair topics with those weaknesses. UWorld percentages are not MCAT score conversions.
If a day is missed, resume today and move only the most important unfinished repair task into the next catch-up slot. Never double the next day automatically.
Full-lengths replace the normal daily checklist and require about 7.5 hours including breaks. Use unused scored exams when possible. Record section scores and whether an exam was repeated.
After each full-length, reassess the January exam using the recent timed score trend. A 510 remains the stretch target; 502–505 is an intermediate goal, not a guarantee.
Khan Academy replaces all textbook content review. Open the listed course/unit and find the exact section heading. Watch only videos, not article items. Section links may open the unit overview.
Video minutes are study budgets, not verified video runtimes. Pause for examples and finish with recall. Resume unfinished sections on their next appearance or during weekly catch-up.
The video boxes are directions for existing checklist tasks, not additional tasks. Later phases use short targeted video repairs so question review keeps priority.
